items.explanation: キャ is 'kya': キ ('ki') plus a small ャ ('ya'), said as one beat. It is the same sound as hiragana きゃ. A combination is an i-column kana followed by a small ゃ, ゅ or ょ, and the two are said together as ONE beat. Size matters: きや (full-size や) is two beats, ki-ya, while きゃ (small ゃ) is one beat, kya.
items.mnemonic: The big キ swallows the little ャ: 'ki' and 'ya' squeeze into one beat, 'kya'.

items.culture_note: Sound-symbolic words are often written in katakana, especially in manga.
